_note: Curated, reasoned endings of catalogue searches (iteration 3, closed-loop demonstration, scientist-b, 2026-10-28). Read by repurposing_join.py handoff. A disposition is a decision about a search, not a claim about biology and not a ranking. Coverage version used: main 315cd50c (before the ABAT / GtoPdb artefact correction of task/it3-search2).

dispositions.subject: apinocaltamide (reverse path: compound without a card -> CACNA1G/H/I -> need)
dispositions.why: ChEMBL curated mechanism (T-type blocker, three subtypes) coherent with a direction-evaluable need; structurally unrelated to ethosuximide, the only drug result of the need. Mechanism-level discriminator only; apinocaltamide sources are abstract-level, adult rodents and healthy adults.
dispositions.reopening_condition: closes if a same-day-controlled Wwox-null pup assay with measured exposure does not reproduce the ethosuximide late-phase effect; weakens if a full-text read shows no brain exposure at pup-relevant conditions
dispositions.next_experiment: Wwox-null pup PTZ late-phase score, three genotypes, concurrent PTZ-alone control, ethosuximide and apinocaltamide arms, exposure measured, pre-planned drug-by-genotype interaction test

dispositions.subject: glycine and aspartic acid (NMDA-receptor agonists)
dispositions.why: Stated action is agonism of GRIN1, GRIN2A and GRIN2B (GtoPdb rows recovered by the iteration-4 identity repair), the opposite sign to a need whose direction is down. Caveats: ChEMBL holds no mechanism row for either compound; the rows are DGIdb / Guide-to-Pharmacology ligand statements, now identity-verified through the GtoPdb ligand and target ids (update 2026-10-29: DGIdb had read the GtoPdb target id as an NCBI Gene id, so the earlier wording that GRIN1 was absent from the record and that the rows came from a family-level propagation pattern is superseded; the rows sit on GRIN1, GRIN2A and GRIN2B and are family-level listings, not subunit-selective statements). The sign is right pharmacologically (aspartate at the glutamate site, glycine as co-agonist) but the classification rests on weak rows; it is not a dose or suitability statement.
dispositions.reopening_condition: a Wwox-deficient system showing NMDA-receptor hypofunction (the need's sign would then be up)
dispositions.next_experiment: none for these compounds; the sign of the need is decided by the MEA / d-APV experiment already named on card F01_glutamate_receptor_node

dispositions.subject: adenosine and regadenoson flagged 'opposed' through ABAT (catalogue records CAT:DGIDB:00b678d594e4 and CAT:DGIDB:bf428fbfbaa3; since the coverage correction these rows are EXCLUDED as source_artefact and no longer in the matrix, which confirms this ending)
dispositions.why: The 'opposed' flag rested on one Guide-to-Pharmacology ligand row 'ABAT agonist' beside a run of unrelated ABC-transporter rows (update 2026-10-29: the cause is the iteration-4 identity finding, not a gene-list expansion or a name collision: DGIdb read the GtoPdb target id as an NCBI Gene id, so a GtoPdb target id of 18, the adenosine A1 receptor, was served as ABAT; after the repair the adenosine and regadenoson rows sit on their true adenosine-receptor targets and no longer on ABAT); the compounds' real pharmacology is at adenosine receptors, which are not targets of this need. Neither an opposite nor a consistent mechanism is established. The compounds' real pharmacology (adenosine receptors) may bear on seizure control through receptors this need does not list; that is not assessed here.
dispositions.reopening_condition: a ChEMBL curated mechanism row or a primary paper stating an action on GABA transaminase
dispositions.next_experiment: none; correct the coverage layer (coordinator task it3-search2)

dispositions.subject: GCN2 (EIF2AK4), from the fly PARS2 reading; DGIdb rows: hesperadin plus five antipsychotics (ziprasidone, olanzapine, haloperidol decanoate, risperidone, quetiapine fumarate; PharmGKB, interaction type unknown)
dispositions.why: Need direction is uncertain, so exploration only. The catalogue holds no ChEMBL mechanism row for EIF2AK4; DGIdb returns five antipsychotics through PharmGKB with interaction type unknown (pharmacogenomic association, not modulation) and hesperadin, a research kinase inhibitor with 81 target rows in the record (EIF2AK4 is one of them, claim source DTC, 'inhibitor'); hesperadin has no row in priorities.json for this need, so search and coverage disagree on it (not resolved here). The only GCN2 datum is genetic suppression in a fly model: genetic suppression is not pharmacology.
dispositions.reopening_condition: (i) phospho-GCN2 / ATF4 elevation in a Wwox-deficient neural system; or (ii) a selective GCN2 modulator, or a ChEMBL curated mechanism row for EIF2AK4, with a stated action. Hesperadin's DTC row does not reopen it: it is one of 81 targets of a multi-kinase compound, a screen-level statement without selectivity or mechanism.
dispositions.next_experiment: in a Wwox-deficient neural system measure phospho-GCN2 versus phospho-PERK with eIF2alpha phosphorylation and ATF4 protein (stage 1 of card E01, plus the kinase question), before any compound

dispositions.subject: pannexin-1 blockers (record Q-N-16) via PANX1
dispositions.why: PANX1 is an intervention target of the need, but the catalogue returns no compound for it (no ChEMBL mechanism row, no DGIdb row). Probenecid, carbenoxolone and brilliant blue G exist in the catalogue under other targets and are not linked by name. Paralogue rows exist: carbenoxolone (CAT:DGIDB:ea45bb50fb31) and flufenamic acid (CAT:DGIDB:37352f589f92) carry Guide-to-Pharmacology 'inhibitor' rows on PANX2 and PANX3; they are not PANX1 evidence and are not used. The only WWOX datum (one slice, one blocker) is a rise in burst frequency, never tested.
dispositions.reopening_condition: a source row linking a catalogue compound to PANX1, or an independent measurement of a pannexin blocker in a Wwox-deficient network
dispositions.next_experiment: independent replication of the slice experiment with a second pannexin-1 blocker and a significance test (record Q-N-16, REPLICATE row)

dispositions.subject: premature-stop read-through agents (ataluren, aminoglycosides, ELX-02) for WWOX nonsense alleles
dispositions.why: The need lists only WWOX as a target, so the catalogue returns no read-through agent through it; agents sit on the ribosome (ChEMBL: ataluren 80S ribosome modulator). Sequence enumeration of 32 ClinVar nonsense alleles: 23 predicted NMD-sensitive, 1 borderline, 8 predicted escape; all five census 'candidate' alleles are NMD-sensitive, and no allele has the UGA-C context. No WWOX read-through or NMD measurement exists. Closest nonsense-DEE trial (ataluren in CDKL5/Dravet, n=15) was negative.
dispositions.reopening_condition: a measured PTC transcript level in patient-derived cells for a recorded WWOX nonsense allele, or any WWOX read-through experiment
dispositions.next_experiment: transcript-level NMD assay (NMD-discriminating arm) on a patient-derived line carrying p.Arg264* or p.Arg54*, and on a predicted-escape allele such as p.Gln353*
